limitations: Delta review of a duplicate-counter rebuild. Reviewer is a same-host AI agent session (model Claude Sonnet 5.5, reviewer_id sonnet-independent-reviewer-copilot) on the same operator account as the producer. Same-host agent reviewer: it is not a second machine, a second operator or a human. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and no repository file, and read only the repository artifacts and the code snapshot /private/tmp/sb-review-d5 (commit ce1670f as stated by the coordinator; the snapshot has no git data, so the commit id was not checked). This review follows the approval of set v9 (copilot-independent-public-review-v9) by the same reviewer id. Delta review: the semantic checks of the previous reviews carry over only for files that are byte-equal to v9; 252 of 278 files are. Set v10 was rebuilt from a new private parent (copilot-score-replay-v6) because the outside review of candidate v39 found two restatements that the duplicate counter missed.

The previous sets must never be published: copilot-public-candidates-v9 states duplicate safety as 7 of 25, 8 of 26 and 6 of 27 and so overstates the score by 0.07 to 0.10 points per run; v8 holds 61 request hashes (262 occurrences) that depend on private text; v7 also holds rewind index keys that were SHA-256 of a private path; older sets hold more. Previous sets that held a private-derived value must never be published. Only v10 may be published. The sidecars beside the packets (summary.json, *-private-transformation.json, *-receipt.json, *-tamper.json) hold digests of private originals and must not be published.

Change of this set, checked by the reviewer. Only the duplicate counter changes. (a) Any text cell of a store table other than turns that holds the complete text of a message is one more occurrence of that message: the cell c0 of search_index_content holds the R1 prompt, a newline and the R1 response (975, 1031 and 1092 characters), so each of the two messages gets one more statement (+2 per run). (b) A tool completion that holds all text arguments of its call restates the call; a call whose only argument is a path (view) is restated only when the completion also states the tool name, and the result text is not counted as that evidence. Each view completion names its path in a diff header and its name in toolTelemetry.properties.command, so it is one more statement of its call (+1 per run). No file of events, store, WAL, rewind snapshots, tracking, inputs, observer, workload or context changes: all 252 equal files include every native and every inputs file. The 26 files that differ are the manifests (size and digests), the receipts and sidecars, the bundle, and five bound runtime files per run (copilot_session_store.py, copilot_format_evidence.py, copilot_density.py, score_replay.py and the adapter document), each equal to the snapshot at ce1670f. Remaining machine detail and judgment. The 1008 vendor hash occurrences (17 prompt segments and 25 tool schemas, 12 characters each) stay because they are equal in all three runs; that proof cannot exclude a constant private value inside the text of a segment (for example a fixed path in host_additional_instructions); the reviewer has no text to test it and judges the segments to be vendor prompt text. Vendor instruction text was blanked at equal raw byte length with the marker [vendor instruction text removed at equal byte length] followed by filler. Vendor-text scan of every file of the three packets, the runtime copies, the replay receipts and the bundle: 40- and 25-character windows of all eight distinct vendor strings of the private parent (system.message content and blocks of all three runs and the MCP instructions), plain and JSON-escaped, gave no hit that is prose. Fixed phrases of the MCP text and eight 40-character phrases of the system prompt: zero hits, also in all text cells and raw pages of the session store (integrity_check ok, 17 tables, native and capture copies). Packet runtime copies: the runtime directory of v10 is the current snapshot (ce1670f) for the five changed files and equal to v9 for the rest. The packets are replayed with the code that was frozen into them; the repository snapshot itself was not replayed. The older-document problem of v9 (the packet document lacked the vendor-text paragraph and carried the old duplicate paragraph) is gone.

The duplicate rule (rubric, Duplicate-safety read, 2026-10-05) was written after the captures and after the earlier approvals. The reviewer recounted from the public native bytes with scripts that import nothing from session_bench (the session store and its WAL were copied to scratch before opening; every text and BLOB cell of every table was searched for the complete text of every prompt, assistant text and reasoning text, every call argument and every result output, also in JSON-escaped form). Events: 16, 17, 16. Statements: events.jsonl 21, 22, 22 (prompts, assistant messages with text or reasoning text, requests, starts, completions) plus one glob completion that holds its pattern in run 3; store turns row 2; rewind index 1; rewind backup 1; search_index_content cell 2; view completion 1. Totals 28, 29, 30. The new counts are right: they are neither too low nor too high. Too low would need a further restatement; none exists: sessions.summary is a truncated prompt (102 characters), workspace.yaml holds no complete prompt, session_files holds the path but names apply_patch (not view), so it does not restate the view call, tool arguments of bash and apply_patch and the result outputs occur in no other cell, the FTS shadow tables other than content hold BLOB terms only, and the virtual table search_index is not read (its text is the same cell, counted once). Too high would need a match that is not a restatement: both new cell matches are complete texts, and the view completion states path and name.

Attack on the containment rule (a text cell holds the message text as a substring, with no minimum length and no word boundary; row_holds_text checks every text cell of the row). In these packets no chance match is possible: the shortest message text that is tested is 206 characters (an assistant answer); the only non-turns cell that holds any message is the 975 to 1092 character cell; the cells of the other tables are session ids, paths, model names, timestamps and token counts, none of which holds a 206-character text. Reasoning texts (387 to 476 characters) occur in no cell. The rule is weak for other data: a message of a few characters (the reviewer's function test: the texts 5, x or the all match the search index cell) would match inside a longer cell and be counted. A minimum length, or equality of a whole cell or of a whole line of a cell, would remove the risk. This does not change these packets, and the row is the same method as the OpenCode row. Judgment on the read (largest item, unchanged): the Copilot row opens the turns table although the decoder takes no scored fact from it; with the cell counted, an OpenCode-style decoder that never parses turns would score 7 of 26, 8 of 27, 6 of 28 (no gain), and one that never opens the store 9 of 24, 10 of 25, 8 of 26 (about 0.3 to 0.4 points more). As built, the decoder opens the store (usage, reconciliation), so the packaged count follows the rule. The rank against Pi rests on small differences under the other reading; this needs an owner decision; the reviewer did not re-score Pi.

The two restatements that v9 missed (search_index_content cell, view completion) are now counted; both were named by the reviewer of v9 and by the outside review of v39. The reviewer found no other missed restatement (see limitation 10).

The glob completion is counted both as the first statement of its own result (useful in density) and as a restatement of its call. This follows the first-record rule; the rule sentence that a duplicate occurrence is never also useful content does not cover a record that states two events.

The alternative of never opening the store is correctly rejected: usage, token semantics and reconciliation would be native_absent (minus 12) for about plus 0.4, and the store is where the harness keeps per-call usage.

Usage hardening requested in the v2 review is implemented and tested by the reviewer: usage credit is refused when the id-joined prompt-cache witness disagrees with the joined store row (count swaps inside one shutdown window, a changed cache count, and the turn-index swap in run 3 all lose the credit). The witness holds no output count, so a changed output count on a displayed row keeps usage credit and fails reconciliation only. A swap of the ids of two tool-call rows is still not detected; those rows are not scored.

Shared-code changes embedded in the packets (comparator tests usage apart from token semantics; rule for unscored native actions; density helpers; the row_holds_text helper) change no other metric row of this configuration. The replay ran the source inside each packet. This reviewer did not rerun the Copilot test files.

The session store was not copied by the capture controller. The producer retrieved session-store.db and session-store.db-wal from the retained temporary roots later on the same day. Acceptance rests on SHA-256 equality with the capture-time receipts: both files equal copilot_home_inventory_after in root-end.json and in the R2 exit receipt, and the reviewer confirmed that those receipt files are byte-equal to the copies inside the earlier v1 packets, which predate the retrieval. The reviewer did not see the temporary roots. session-store.db-shm was not copied (a read-only open before the retrieval rewrote it). It is a rebuildable WAL index: every frame of each WAL is checksum-valid with the header salts, the last frame is a commit frame, and SQLite reads the same rows without it.

The store holds only the scored session because COPILOT_HOME was new and empty (one sessions row, one session id in every table, main database file is one empty page). In normal use the store is shared by all sessions of a home, so a single session cannot be copied as files without other sessions. The same limit applies to the OpenCode database row. config.json, settings.json and logs/ of COPILOT_HOME were hash-listed and not copied; the reviewer could not check the statement that they hold no session records.

Usage join without a shared id. A usage row has session_id, turn_index and an autoincrement id, and no event id. The decoder joins the rows of one turn_index in id order to the assistant.message events of the user turn with that ordinal, and only when the counts are equal, the position equals the native turnId, the models are equal and finish_reason agrees. The reviewer judges this exact enough for the two scored responses of each run for these reasons: the displayed response is the only row of its turn with finish_reason stop and the only message of its turn without tool requests; the store turns row binds turn_index 0 to the exact R1 prompt and R1 response text; session.usage_checkpoint, joined to the displayed response by a real shared id (model_call_id = apiCallId), holds prompt_tokens, cache_read and cache_write that equal the joined row and no other row, in all six cases; created_at is 3 to 6 ms before the message timestamp in all 22 rows (not used as a key). The shared comparator accepts a turn-level usage join for every configuration, so this join is not weaker than the common rule. It is weaker than the Codex and Claude rows, where the usage record carries or sits inside the response record.

Token semantics. The columns are nullable integers; the decoder keeps 0 and NULL distinct and a NULL count loses credit (reviewer mutation). input_tokens includes cached tokens (for example 13413 = 3 uncached + 0 read + 13410 written); token_details_json holds the billed counts per token type. Credit follows the shared shape rule (input, output, cache read and cache write present as integers). The name input_tokens alone does not say that it includes cache tokens; the adapter document says it. Only the two displayed responses per run are scored for usage, as for every configuration.

Reconciliation was recomputed by the reviewer from the public store against both session.shutdown records of each run: request count, input, output, cache read, cache write, reasoning, totalNanoAiu and the four tokenDetails counts are all equal (3 and 7, 3 and 7, 4 and 8 rows).

The public session-store.db-wal is a derivative. The temporary directory id inside the pages is aliased at equal length (13 places per run) and the frame checksums are recomputed. The reviewer confirmed: every byte that differs from the private WAL is inside an aliased path or a frame checksum field; a stock SQLite reader on a scratch copy returns integrity_check ok, no free pages and the private rows with only the alias applied; there are no frames after the valid ones and no bytes after the last frame; the full-text index vocabulary holds only words of the public event text. A public reader cannot verify the private checksums. Digests of the store in the public receipts were rewritten to the public bytes; the digest of the uncopied -shm file and of the R1-state WAL are zeroed.

Version judgment. The declared version is events=1;session-store=8: session.start.data.version and the store table schema_version, both integers separate from the application build. The decoder refuses another value of either (reviewer mutations). Builds 1.0.89 and 1.0.91 hold the same values and an identical store schema. Only one value of each was ever observed, so the claim that the version distinguishes incompatible schemas is not tested by a second value.

The file-change timestamp is the snapshot record's own timestamp (about 2.5 s after the edit result), accepted as in v1 (0.15 points). Run 3 has a different post-image hash than runs 1 and 2 because the model wrote a different edit; native snapshot, patch replay and observer agree in each run.

The packet manifests, replay receipts and the producer summary still say public_safe: false and independent_reproduction: false. This review is an attestation by an agent; it does not change those fields and is not an independent reproduction on a second environment.
